title: Six-class (negation + GLV) parallel Pollard rho on secp256k1 with a global work meter, tightened accounting (v2g)

claims.statement: For the uniform full-production secp256k1 target Q=[x]P, the classical cold attack in proof.md (six-class negation+GLV parallel Pollard rho: twisted R=2048 adding walk on classes keyed by |y|, exact 4-limb truncated canonical-index rule with metered fallback, doubling escapes from detected 2-cycles and checkpoint cycles of length <= 64, distinguished classes routed to 2^16 storage nodes each natively addressable below 2^56 bytes, re-walk solving), ported from submission 1c600df4 (mpjunior92, BLS12-381 G1) with secp256k1 constants and prices; this v2g (provenance: the declared dependency 189ebc42; all bounds restated and re-verified in this package) tightens three accounting constants only (step charge 1.18 over the published 159-instruction itemisation, 4% slowdown allowance, H1 quantile floor 0.396), halts on every run after at most 2^127.025 target-group-operation equivalents (one unit = one batched incomplete affine secp256k1 addition, C=1000) because a global work meter charges every action before it runs. It succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed heuristic H1 (random mapping on N=(r-1)/6 classes with Brent-Pollard correction and a 4% slowdown allowance; partition, distinguished and routing bits pseudo-random), supported by toy runs. Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing <= 2^59.0 units, enforced and included; no nonuniform advice. Not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of every identity the walk uses and of the truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: the complete per-trail algorithm on prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3+7 (T_c census, pipeline success with node routing, long-trail trap test).
